why: Lines 1-5 give a date, a death, a blackout and a dead dog. It is creepy and I want to know if it is real. Line 6 connects it to a pharaoh's tomb.
first_moment_I_got_curious: Line 3-4 (blackout, then the dog howls and dies)
where_I_would_swipe_away: Lines 17-19: Times of London exclusive rights and other reporters. It is a media-business detail and the pace drops.
Lines 27-29: the 25 people, 70 vs 75 average. It is a stats lecture, though short.
lines_I_did_not_understand: 20-22: who is 科雷利 and who is 'she'? The pronoun comes without warning.
24: which prince, and why is he here? It comes out of nowhere.
37: 'it' is the tomb, but that is not obvious. Why is it ironic?
11: 5000 items is just a number and does not connect to the story.
takeaway_in_my_words: The curse was made up by newspapers. Carnarvon died of an infected mosquito bite, and a good story spread faster than the truth.
surprise_that_stuck: The dog actually died 4 hours later, so the 'same moment' detail was false. Also, real ancient curses exist ('wring his neck like a goose'), but Tutankhamun's tomb has none.
title_I_would_click: 法老的诅咒是真的吗？ It is a direct question and I want to know the answer.
what_I_would_comment: So the dog dying was fake too? LOL. I would go in, but I would bring mosquito repellent.
